questions.prompt: Loose callers on your left, you are under the gun with KJo at 100bb. Compared with a tight table, you should…

choices.text: Open less often. You will be called and dominated.
Open wider. Callers make KJo stronger.
Limp. Loose tables require limps from UTG.

questions.explanation: When the field calls too much, remove dominated offsuit hands from early opens.

questions.prompt: Same loose table, button, folded to you with KJo. Now…

choices.text: Fold. The button uses the UTG range.
Open. Position and their calling still favor a late steal that can win immediately or play in position.

questions.explanation: The same hand changes with seat. Button versus blinds is not UTG versus a calling field.

questions.prompt: You cover the table with 300bb. A short stack with 20bb open-jams. With QQ you…

choices.text: Call only if you also cover a third stack of 300bb
Call the 20bb. Your extra chips behind do not change this pot.

questions.explanation: Effective stack is the jam, 20bb, not the 300bb you cannot win.

questions.prompt: The table is 4-handed at 100bb. Your earliest open should look more like…

choices.text: A full-ring cutoff or button range, not a full-ring UTG range

questions.explanation: Four-handed has no true early position. Opening the 9-handed UTG chart is far too tight.
